tiers.title: Grab first: medical and must-haves
tiers.hint: If you only have a few minutes, this is it.

fixed.text: **Insulin: out of the fridge and into the travel cooler.** Take all of it, the vials or pens in use and the spares.
fixed.note: Keep it cool, never frozen, and out of direct sun. The guide covers keeping it cool on the road and at Gram's.

fixed.text: **Pump, CGM and the phone that runs the CGM app.** Take everything the person is using now, plus every charger.
fixed.note: Pack the backup supplies with them: spare pods, cartridges or infusion sets, and a way to inject insulin (syringes or pen needles) if the pump fails.

fixed.text: **Glucagon and fast sugar in a pocket**, not packed in a bag.
fixed.note: Check the glucagon is in date, and make sure the family knows where it is.

fixed.text: The rest of the **T1D go-kit**: meter, test strips, lancets, ketone strips, spare batteries, alcohol wipes and a container for used needles.
fixed.note: Skip any line you already ticked from the inventory below.

fixed.text: **Written T1D plan and prescription copies**, in a sealed bag.
fixed.note: Print the saved plan from this app. Add the medicine doses and times, pharmacy and doctor contacts, and the make and model of the pump and CGM.

fixed.text: **Medical ID** (bracelet or necklace) on the person with diabetes.
fixed.note: It speaks for them if they cannot.

fixed.text: **Every household member's medications.**
fixed.note: The app lists each person's medications below. Take the medicines themselves and a written list of doses.

fixed.text: Phones and charging cables.
fixed.note: Charge them before you leave if you still have power.

fixed.text: Wallet, keys, ID and cash.
Copies of insurance papers, IDs and bank records, in a waterproof container.
Glasses or contacts, and contact lens solution.
**Pets**, with leashes or carriers.
fixed.note: Most public shelters take only service animals, so the plan is to take them with you to Gram's.

fixed.text: **Solar generator(s): grab them, plus every charging cable.**
fixed.note: If you still have power while you pack, top them up first.

fixed.text: **Solar panels: fold them, and bring their cables and connectors.**
fixed.note: The cable that joins the panels to the generator is the easiest thing to leave behind.

fixed.text: Power banks, charged.
**Meshtastic radios**, charged, with their charging cables.
FRS radios, charged, with chargers or spare batteries.
**Weather radio** (battery-powered), with spare batteries.
Flashlights and extra batteries.
A **printed copy of this binder**.
fixed.note: Print it while you have power: More, then Print binder. Keep it with the go-bags.

fixed.text: **Water containers, filled.**
fixed.note: Ready.gov says plan one gallon per person per day, for several days.

fixed.text: Water filter.
fixed.note: Pack its cleaning or backflush parts too.

fixed.text: Bleach for treating water: plain, unscented.
fixed.note: The guide shows how much to use.

fixed.text: **Food for at least the trip**, plus non-perishable food beyond that.
Pet food and water for the pets.
fixed.note: A several-day supply in an airtight, waterproof container, plus a water bowl.

fixed.text: First aid kit.
Camp stove and fuel.
fixed.note: Cook outdoors only, never inside a home or garage. See the carbon monoxide guide.

fixed.text: Sleeping bag or warm blanket for each person.
A complete change of clothes for each person, and sturdy shoes.
Sanitation supplies: moist towelettes, garbage bags, plastic ties, soap and hand sanitizer.
Personal hygiene items.
Basic tools: wrench or pliers, scissors and duct tape.
Whistle and dust masks.
Matches in a waterproof container.
Paper maps of the area and the routes to Gram's.
